finding.claim: Tokens with a missing or unknown kid trigger an uncached JWKS refresh (outbound HTTP fetch) on every call, with no rate limit or negative cache. Low severity: refresh-on-miss is intentional and documented, so this is request amplification, not a verification bypass.
finding.source: Token header kid (absent or unknown), read unverified in PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt at jwt/jwks_client.py:239-241
finding.sink: PyJWKClient.get_signing_keys(refresh=True) -> fetch_data() outbound request at jwt/jwks_client.py:218 -> :163-168 (cache bypassed) -> :130-135

trace.note: header.get('kid') passed through; None when absent
match_kid on cached set; None or unknown kid never matches (:257)
opener.open(r, timeout=30) issues a network request per such token

finding.guards_checked: kid type-checked only when present (api_jws.py:441-448), so a missing kid skips it and reaches refresh. No rate limit, negative cache, or single-flight lock. Redirects disabled (jwks_client.py:17-27) and scheme limited to http/https (:90-95), so destination is fixed to the configured JWKS URI; no attacker control over the target.
